newsitem.title: USA: Calif. crime rate drops 12 pct; murders down 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Calif. crime rate drops 12 pct; murders down 18 pct.

text.p: Crime in California's most populated areas dropped more than 12 percent last year compared to 1995, the largest one year drop ever, according to a state report released Wednesday.
State Attorney General Dan Lungren said the finidngs showed that California's "Three Strikes" anti-crime law, which mandates stiff prison sentences for repeat offenders, was working.
The number of murders reported decreased 18.4 percent, according the preliminary state report for 1996.
"We need to understand the magnitude of what is happening in California," Lungren said. "We are not simply tagging along with the rest of the country. We are outpacing it."

The report found that violent crime decreased 10 percent in number in the state. The number of homicides reported for 1996 decreased 18.4 percent, while the number of rapes decreased 4.3 percent in 1996 from 1995.

Property crime decreased 13.3 percent in number, the report found. In 1996, the number of reported burglaries decreased 12.3 percent compared to 1995. There was a 14.5 percent decrease in the number of motor vehicle thefts reported in 1996 compared to 1995.
The report compared preliminary counts of crimes for 1996 with those of 1995 for jurisdictions with a population of 100,000 or more.
Over the last three years, homicides in the state have dropped by more than 30 percent, Lungren's office said.
"Had the level of homicides since 1993 continued unabated, some 2,100 people would no longer be alive," Lungren said. "That's a stunning reality."
